title: Sprint checkpoint — Console & Tooling (UI / Rollouts / Analytics)
body:
Sprint checkpoint notes — quick capture (mixed formal/informal).

Date: 2026-03-30
Attendees: Maya, Liam, Sofia, Ethan, Priya, (quick ping: Alex on PTO)
Timebox: 45m standup-style checkpoint + 20m deep dive on analytics gaps

Purpose: consolidate blockers & decisions before rollout window next Tue 2026-04-06. Focus areas: rollout UX polish for preview + canary traffic shaping, analytics event gaps impacting regression detection, and short-term mitigations for visible preview flicker.

---
Key outcomes (TL;DR):
- Agreed to ship a hotfix for preview render jitter (client fallback) by EOD 2026-04-01 (owner: Liam).
- Deferring the full rollout orchestration refactor to next sprint; will instead add a safety flag and expanded telemetry to reduce risk.
- Identified three missing analytics events preventing automated quality regression alerts; prioritized instrumentation tickets and temporary manual checks.

Meeting notes (by topic)

1) UI / Preview flicker (severity: medium-high)
- Symptom: when a canary rollout is active and model variant metadata is large, preview component reflows intermittently during the initial render (~100–400ms).
- Root cause hypothesis: previews call model-metadata endpoint synchronously during component mount; large response triggers long main-thread parsing + layout thrash when combined with canvas drawing for diffs.
- Recent regression: introduced metadata fields for quantization profile in PR #1198 which expanded payloads.
- Short-term mitigation (agreed):
  - Serve a trimmed preview payload via /preview-lite for initial render (Liam to implement proxy; ETA 2026-04-01).
  - Client changes: show skeleton and render full metadata asynchronously with graceful color/height hints (Sofia to ship small client patch; ETA 2026-04-01).
  - Add flaky metric (preview-flicker-rate) to the rollout dashboard (Ethan to add event and dashboard tile; ETA 2026-04-02).
- Longer-term: decouple preview rendering from heavy metadata, move to delta streaming model. Add to backlog as "preview-streaming-refactor" (priority: P2).

2) Rollouts orchestration + canary shaping
- Problem statement: traffic split logic does not currently account for sequence length distribution; some high-latency tails get routed to canaries causing SLA blips.
- Quick trade: we can either block routing by seq-len on the router (more invasive) or add a smarter predictor that rejects heavy sequences for canary traffic (lighter).
- Decision: add a lightweight pre-routing heuristic in the control plane that tags requests with "canary-eligible:false" if estimated token budget > 1024. This reduces canary exposure to heavy workloads while we scope a longer-term router refactor. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2026-04-05 (config only).
- Action: add documentation entry in rollout playbook describing the heuristic and how to opt-in for experiments. (Priya to draft).

3) Analytics gaps — blocking quality/regression alerts
- Found three missing events that block automated comparison between baseline and canary:
  - early_stop_reason (missing in some code paths)
  - token_generation_latency.bucket (no consistent bucketization across variants)
  - model_variant_tag (missing in async worker responses)
- Work items:
  - RWN-4380: instrument early_stop_reason at source for streaming and batch paths (owner: Ethan; ETA 2026-04-02).
  - RWN-4391: standardize latency bucketing utility in shared telemetry lib (owner: Sofia; ETA 2026-04-04).
  - RWN-4393: propagate model_variant_tag through async worker headers (owner: Maya; ETA 2026-04-03).
- Temporary manual check: add a daily smoke job that samples 100 requests from canary and baseline and dumps relevant fields to a Slack batch for ops until alerts are healthy (Liam + SRE).

4) Canary fallback rehearsals & runbook updates
- Next Friday will run a rehearsal: partial failover to fallback model variant and validate latency/cost metrics + client behavior. (Schedule: 2026-04-09 09:00 PST).
- Runbook changes needed:
  - clarify steps to toggle safety flag (new UI toggle planned by ProdOps).
  - add checklist for verifying telemetry keys after toggle.
- Owner for runbook edits: Priya (will coordinate with solutions-eng).

5) UX / console observability improvements
- New dashboard requirements captured: per-variant token cost trend, preview-flicker heatmap, canary-eligible traffic % by route. Ethan to sketch tile mockups and post in #console-rollouts for quick feedback.
- Quick wins: add hover tooltips showing last-deployed-commit for a model variant (low lift). Owner: Sofia.

6) Risks & open questions
- Risk: adding heuristics may bias traffic away from realistic distribution; we must avoid overfitting the canary population. Mitigation: rotate canary eligibility window and sample slices daily. (Priya + Data team to propose schedule).
- Open Q: do we retry on preview-lite fetch failure or fallback to full preview? (UX decision) — defer to product; Sophia recommended retry with exponential backoff + analytics tag.
- Pending infra constraint: the private deployment customers with older routing libs may not honor canary-eligible tag. Need compatibility check. (Action: Maya to compile customer list and impacts; ETA 2026-04-04).

Action items (short list)
- Liam: implement preview-lite proxy + quick server-side trim. ETA 2026-04-01. linked: PR stub exists.
- Sofia: client skeleton + async metadata render. ETA 2026-04-01.
- Ethan: add preview-flicker-rate event + dashboard tile. ETA 2026-04-02.
- Maya: propagate model_variant_tag in async workers. ETA 2026-04-03.
- Priya: pre-routing heuristic config + rollout playbook entry. ETA 2026-04-05.
- All: sign up for rehearsal on 2026-04-09; owners to prep checklists by 2026-04-07.

Notes to self / stream-of-consciousness (ok to be messy)
- need to check if preview-lite will increase requests to metadata store (caching?). Maybe better to cache trimmed view at CDN edge for 10m. cheap perf win.
- consider reusing existing cost telemetry labels rather than inventing preview-flicker metric if we can repurpose something. but specific tag helps alerting.
- possible followup: add a small experiment flag to force 0% canary for seq_len>1024 in staging for a week, see whether it reduces flakiness.

Decisions for product review (explicit asks)
- Product to confirm: happy with preview-lite UX or want full preview on first paint? (impact: quick fix vs bigger change).
- Product to confirm: are we allowed to change routing heuristics by seq-len for public hosted customers? Need legal/ops signoff for private deployments.

Misc links / references mentioned in meeting:
- Linear: RWN-4322, RWN-4380, RWN-4391, RWN-4393
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1198 (metadata payload changes)
- Slack thread: #console-rollouts "preview jitter" (2026-03-29)

Next checkpoint: quick async update on progress 2026-04-02 morning; full sprint review in our normal weekly on 2026-04-06.

Draft-ends — put comments inline below if you were in the meeting.
